name: Santana Minerals Limited
overview: Santana Minerals is a pre-revenue gold exploration and development company dual-listed on the ASX (primary) and NZX, reporting in AUD with a 30-June fiscal year. Its sole material asset is the Bendigo-Ophir Gold Project (BOGP) in Central Otago, New Zealand — an open-pit-then-underground development centred on the Rise & Shine (RAS) deposit, with satellite deposits Come In Time (CIT), Srex (SRX) and Srex-East (SRE) — for which an Updated Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS, July 2025) outlines a 1.24Moz JORC Ore Reserve and a 13.8-year initial mine life. The company has no operating mine, no revenue and no offtake; its entire value is a claim on future cash flows contingent on permitting, financing and construction that have not yet occurred.

business_model.summary: Santana earns no revenue. It is a capital-consuming exploration/development vehicle funded entirely by equity issuance (and prospectively project debt), whose economic value is embedded in the PFS-modelled future cash flows of the Bendigo-Ophir Gold Project once (if) it is permitted, financed and built. There are no recurring revenue streams — the business model is 'de-risk the project, then either build it (diluting/leveraging the balance sheet) or sell/partner it to a producer.'

revenue_streams.name: Gold sales (BOGP, not yet producing)
revenue_streams.trend: pre-revenue; targeted first gold ~2028 per company guidance, subject to consent

business_model.customer_type: None currently — future customer base would be gold refiners/bullion banks off-take on a spot/hedged basis once in production
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand (Central Otago, single project); corporate domicile/listing split Australia (ASX primary) and New Zealand (NZX secondary)

main_competitors: OceanaGold (operates the nearby Macraes mine, ~90km away, and Waihi — the benchmark NZ gold operator)
Federation Mining / Reefton (NZ West Coast gold developer)
Other ASX/TSX junior gold developers competing for the same generalist and specialist gold-development capital (e.g., De Grey Mining precedent, Ora Banda, Genesis Minerals as re-rating comparables)
Global gold miners more broadly for investor capital allocation as gold price beneficiaries (Newmont, Barrick, Northern Star, Evolution)
competitive_position.market_position: Advanced-stage single-asset gold developer, not yet a producer; would become New Zealand's largest new gold mine in decades and a material addition to the country's small gold-mining sector (alongside OceanaGold) if built

moat_factors.description: 2.34Moz combined JORC Mineral Resource at 2.1g/t and a 1.24Moz Probable Ore Reserve at 2.58g/t is large and high-grade by New Zealand standards, and freehold-land tenure (with royalty buy-backs underway) simplifies future development versus competing for Crown/DOC land

No FIFO/airstrip required, grid-connected low-cost hydro power (Clyde Dam ~5km away), sealed highway access, and proximity to Cromwell/Queenstown labour markets support a genuinely lower operating-cost structure than remote developments

Direct listing in the Fast-track Approvals Act 2024 was intended to bypass normal referral stages, but repeated timeline extensions (30 to 60 to 110-120 working days) show this advantage has been only partially realised in practice

~380 sq km of tenure across the historic Otago Goldfields with 30km of prospective strike and multiple untested soil anomalies (DNS, ORK) provides call-option-like exploration upside beyond the current Reserve

weaknesses: Single-asset, single-jurisdiction concentration — all value depends on one deposit and one regulatory process succeeding
No moat in the traditional sense: gold is a commodity, and the project's economics are entirely a function of grade, cost and gold price rather than any pricing power or customer relationship
No construction or operating track record — management has never built or run a mine of this scale
Dependent on external financiers (equity market and prospective project lenders) for the ~A$277m pre-production capex, with no committed debt facility as of the most recent filings

growth_drivers: Receipt of Fast-track Approvals Act consent (decision currently targeted 16 December 2026) unlocking construction and re-rating the stock from an option-value to a funded-developer valuation
Completion of project debt financing alongside existing cash to close the ~A$277m pre-production capex funding gap without excessive equity dilution
Ramp to first gold (company-targeted 2028) and then to steady-state ~120,000oz/year production over a 13.8-year initial mine life

Resource growth from ongoing drilling at RAS North (down-plunge extension, high-grade intercepts) and untested regional targets across 380 sq km of tenure, which could extend mine life or lift throughput (optionality to expand the plant from 1.2Mtpa to 1.8Mtpa)

Gold price strength — spot gold (~A$5,900-6,200/oz as of Sep 2026) is running well above both the PFS base case (A$3,500/oz) and the PFS 'current price' case (A$4,950/oz), materially increasing modelled project NPV if consent is secured
Land consolidation and royalty buy-backs (Bendigo Station, Ardgour Station freehold acquisitions, OIO consent obtained May 2026) simplifying the ownership structure and improving project economics

Potential value-realisation alternatives flagged by the company itself — divesting a royalty/streaming interest or a partial/full sale of the project — which could crystallise value without full-scale equity/debt-funded construction risk

business.description: 100% of company value rests on the Bendigo-Ophir project; there is no diversification if the project is delayed, scaled back, or fails technically/commercially
Management has advanced the project through study phases but has not yet built or operated a mine of this scale in New Zealand's regulatory environment

business.risk: Inferred resource in the mine plan
business.description: Approximately 7% of tonnes in the PFS production target are in the lower-confidence Inferred Resource category; there is no certainty this converts to Indicated/Measured or that the production target is realised

financial.risk: Funding gap for A$277m pre-production capex
financial.description: Cash of ~A$90-190m (varying by quarter, after successive raises) covers only a portion of the PFS pre-production capex; the balance is expected from project debt and/or further equity, with terms and availability not yet locked in. Company's own disclosures warn financing may be dilutive or otherwise adversely impact shareholder value, and note it is exploring alternatives including divesting revenue streams or a partial/full project sale

Company has repeatedly tapped equity markets (A$64.2m gross in H1 FY2026, a further A$130m placement at A$0.90/share plus a A$4.1m SPP in Feb 2026); further large raises are likely needed to fund construction, diluting existing holders
Lender technical due diligence and an Independent Technical Expert appointment are underway but no binding project finance facility has been announced as of the latest filings

regulatory.risk: Fast-track consent may be refused, delayed further, or conditioned heavily
regulatory.description: The single biggest binary risk to the thesis. The statutory decision window has already been extended multiple times (an initial 30 working days, extended to 60, with the independent panel convenor proposing 110-120 working days); the decision date has moved from an original expectation to 29 October 2026 and then to 16 December 2026 in the most recent company presentation. There is no guarantee of a further slip or of an outright refusal/heavily conditioned consent

regulatory.risk: Treaty of Waitangi / iwi consultation challenge
regulatory.description: Four Otago iwi authorities have raised concerns that pre-lodgement consultation was inadequate and alleged potential Treaty breaches; the panel chair has acknowledged the argument that this could foreclose the process under section 7 of the Fast-track Act, with commentators noting the entire application could in principle be voided

Prominent opponents (actor Sam Neill, former PM Helen Clark, the Environmental Defence Society) have publicly campaigned against the mine, citing risks to the Clutha catchment (tailings dam), regional tourism and wine industry branding, and long-duration environmental effects; this raises political/reputational risk even within a fast-track framework designed to limit such challenges

regulatory.risk: Mining permit vs. full consent gap
regulatory.description: A 30-year Mining Permit (MMP 61326) has been granted by NZPAM, but this is a tenure/rights instrument, not the substantive environmental/resource consent required to actually mine — that decision remains pending under the Fast-track Approvals Act

macro.description: Project NPV is extremely sensitive to gold price (PFS tornado analysis shows +/-10% gold price moves NPV by roughly +/-A$179m against an ~A$780m base-case NPV — the single largest sensitivity of any variable); the current re-rate thesis depends heavily on gold holding well above the A$3,500/oz PFS base case

Costs and capex are substantially NZD-denominated (mine in NZ) while the company reports in AUD and gold is priced in USD; the PFS shows materially different outcomes (e.g., NPV of A$1,662m in NZD terms vs A$1,521m in AUD terms at the same underlying scenario) purely from FX translation

The A$277m pre-production capex estimate carries a 10% contingency and is stated to +/-15% accuracy; global mine construction cost inflation (labour, steel, cement, mining fleet) could erode this buffer before financing is locked in

The stock has traded in a wide 52-week range (~NZ$0.495 to NZ$1.395) reflecting its optionality and event-driven repricing around permitting news; dual ASX/NZX listing with modest daily liquidity (~2.8m shares/day per company disclosure) amplifies moves

execution.description: The company has already publicly missed its own earlier submission timeline for the Fast-track application (acknowledged and apologised for by the Chairman in the FY2025 annual report) due to a shortage of specialist consultants in New Zealand; further slippage in construction readiness, financing close, or first-gold timing (company guides 2028) is a realistic risk

The board and executive team (Cook, Bunting, Scotney, Spring, Smith, McPherson) have strong finance/legal/mining-engineering credentials for the study phase, but transitioning to construction and operating management of a A$277m, 120,000oz/year mine is a materially different execution challenge

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold mining/development sector benefiting from a strong multi-year gold bull market; spot gold trades around A$5,900-6,200/oz as of September 2026, well above the PFS base case (A$3,500/oz) and even above the PFS 'current price' scenario struck in mid-2025 (A$4,950/oz), which mechanically inflates modelled project economics for any developer able to reach production. New Zealand's Fast-track Approvals Act 2024 was designed to shorten permitting timelines for nationally significant projects, creating a broader tailwind for NZ resource developments, though Santana's own experience shows practical implementation has been slower and more contested than the legislation's stated intent
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — as a pre-revenue developer, the stock is a leveraged, event-driven proxy on (1) the gold price and (2) discrete regulatory/financing catalysts, rather than a steady operating cyclical
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirect sensitivity: higher rates increase the discount rate applied to the PFS NPV (project modelled at 6.5% — itself already reduced from 8% in the prior PFS to reflect 'de-risking'), raise the cost of prospective project debt, and are a general headwind to non-yielding gold and speculative developer equities generally
macro_factors.currency_exposure: AUD reporting entity with NZD-denominated project costs/capex and USD-denominated gold price exposure — a three-currency structure that adds volatility to reported project economics independent of underlying operating performance
key_input_costs: Steel, cement and construction labour for the process plant and tailings dam
Specialist environmental/regulatory consulting capacity (identified by the company itself as a bottleneck)

recent_developments.event: Updated Pre-Feasibility Study released: after-tax NPV6.5 of A$780m at a A$3,500/oz base case (39% IRR) and A$1.52bn at a then-current A$4,950/oz gold price (65% IRR); pre-production capex reduced to A$277m; mine life extended to 13.8 years for 1.25Moz production; Ore Reserve of 15.0Mt @ 2.58g/t Au for 1.242Moz established

Fast-track Approvals Act (FTA) application lodged and formally accepted by the Environmental Protection Authority (November 2025); a 30-year Mining Permit (MMP 61326) granted by NZPAM over the RAS deposit and satellites

A$64.2m gross raised; binding conditional agreements executed to acquire freehold land at Bendigo and Ardgour Stations plus associated royalty buy-backs; early site works (raw water pipeline, access upgrades) commenced; Independent Technical Expert appointed and lender technical due diligence begun
A$130m two-tranche institutional placement completed at A$0.90/share, plus a A$4.1m Share Purchase Plan — materially diluting the share count to fund development readiness and the financing runway
Overseas Investment Office (OIO) consent granted for the purchase of approximately 3,680 hectares of freehold farmland supporting the project footprint

The Fast-track decision timeline has repeatedly extended — from an initially anticipated ~30 working days, to 60 working days, with the independent panel convenor (a former Environment Court judge) proposing 110-120 working days; the decision date has moved in company/regulatory disclosures from an earlier expectation to 29 October 2026 and, most recently (per the August 2026 Diggers and Dealers presentation), to a Final Decision due 16 December 2026, with a November 2026 draft decision

High-profile public opposition intensified, including actor Sam Neill and former PM Helen Clark, plus formal concerns from four Otago iwi authorities alleging inadequate pre-lodgement consultation and potential Treaty of Waitangi breaches that could, in principle, void the application under section 7 of the Fast-track Act; this uncertainty is the leading explanation for the share price falling from a 52-week high of NZ$1.395 to around NZ$0.62 despite a rising gold price and continued project de-risking

Diggers and Dealers presentation reaffirmed guidance for first gold in 2028, cited net cash of ~A$185m, market capitalisation of ~A$465m, and a base-case (A$3,500/oz) NPV of A$2.1bn after tax at a A$6,000/oz spot-adjusted scenario — underscoring the gold-price leverage of the outstanding-approval thesis

guidance.as_of: Diggers and Dealers Presentation, August 2026 (updating the July 2025 Updated PFS)

items.vs_prior: pushed back from an earlier 29 October 2026 date disclosed in the H1 FY2026 half-year report, itself later than original expectations of a much shorter (30-60 working day) statutory window
items.notes: Draft decision guided for November 2026; RFI response processes ongoing through August 2026

items.vs_prior: consistent with company messaging since the PFS, contingent entirely on receiving consent by end-2026 and financing close shortly after
items.notes: Implies bulk pre-strip commencing ~June 2027 and earthworks ~February 2027 per the presentation's own path-to-production schedule

items.vs_prior: reduced from the November 2024 PFS estimate via plant redesign (1.2Mtpa 3-stage crush/ball mill vs original 1.5Mtpa SAG mill) and lower pre-strip requirements (6.5Mbcm vs 15Mbcm)
items.notes: Total capex over the mine life (including sustaining and underground development capex) is A$487m; financing plan combines existing cash (~A$185-190m as of mid-2026) with prospective project debt, and further equity cannot be ruled out

items.target: ~120,000oz per annum in peak years; 1.25Moz over a 13.8-year initial mine life
items.period: Life of mine, post first gold (2028)
items.vs_prior: increased from the November 2024 PFS (1.15Moz over 9.2 years) via the March 2025 Mineral Resource Estimate upgrade and mine plan refinement
items.notes: Plant designed with expansion optionality to 1.8Mtpa, which management flags could increase annual ounces and bring forward production, but this is not in the base PFS case

items.target: A$1,660/oz (base case, A$3,500/oz gold) to A$1,842/oz (at higher realised gold price scenario, due to profit-linked Crown royalty)
items.vs_prior: maintained from the July 2025 Updated PFS
items.notes: AISC is inversely counter-intuitive versus gold price because the 10% Accounting Profit Royalty (APR) payable to the Crown rises with realised price, above the 2% NSR floor

items.target: A$780m at base case A$3,500/oz (6.5% discount rate); A$2.1bn at spot-referenced ~A$6,000/oz gold price per the August 2026 presentation
items.period: Project life, from PFS effective date
items.vs_prior: materially raised versus the November 2024 PFS due to the gold price rally and lower capex; the A$2.1bn figure is management's own updated illustrative scenario at a higher spot gold price, not a formally re-issued PFS/DFS
items.notes: PFS-derived figures (A$780m / A$1.52bn) are the technically documented JORC-compliant scenarios; the A$2.1bn figure should be treated as indicative management commentary on gold-price sensitivity, not a re-audited study outcome

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Peter Cook has publicly apologised to shareholders for missing earlier Fast-track submission timelines, attributing delays to a shortage of specialist consulting capacity in New Zealand, while maintaining that Fast-track 'does not mean short cut' and that the rigour of the process remains high. CEO Damian Spring has pushed back publicly against panel proposals to extend the statutory decision window, arguing a robust application should support a faster decision, and has reaffirmed a first-gold target of 2028 (previously communicated as feasible under statutory timeframes even before the most recent extension to 16 December 2026). The company has explicitly flagged to shareholders that project financing may require dilutive equity or debt on adverse terms, and that alternative value-realisation strategies — including a royalty/stream sale or a partial/full sale of the project — remain under consideration.

bull_case: Large, high-grade (2.58g/t Reserve grade) gold deposit with low-cost infrastructure advantages (grid hydro power, sealed road access, no FIFO) supports genuinely low operating costs (~A$1,660-1,842/oz AISC) relative to global peers

Extreme gold-price leverage: spot gold (~A$5,900-6,200/oz) is running far above both the PFS base case (A$3,500/oz) and prior 'current price' scenario (A$4,950/oz), meaning even partial de-risking (consent granted) could support a large re-rate from the current ~NZ$0.62 price toward analyst targets clustered around A$1.6-1.75

Strong balance sheet for a developer — net cash of roughly A$185-190m as of mid-2026 with essentially no debt, funded by successive well-supported capital raises, reducing near-term liquidity/going-concern risk while the consent process plays out

Substantial exploration upside beyond the current Reserve — ~380 sq km of underexplored tenure, 30km of prospective strike, and continuing high-grade drill results at RAS North (down-plunge extension) that could extend mine life or lift production beyond the current 13.8-year/1.25Moz plan

A successful Fast-track consent (next major catalyst, currently guided for 16 December 2026) would resolve the single largest overhang and is the type of binary de-risking event that historically re-rates junior gold developers sharply upward toward NPV-based valuations
bear_case: Permitting is genuinely uncertain, not merely a formality: the decision timeline has already slipped multiple times (30 to 60 to a proposed 110-120 working days), and iwi Treaty-of-Waitangi consultation concerns raised before the panel could, on the company's own disclosed risk factors and independent commentary, result in further delay or even void the application

The A$277m (A$487m life-of-mine) capital requirement against current cash of under A$200m implies a large incremental funding need — likely a mix of further dilutive equity issuance (the company has already raised well over A$150m in less than 12 months, including a A$130m placement in Feb 2026) and as-yet-uncommitted project debt on terms not yet disclosed

Zero revenue and no operating history: this is a call option on a regulatory decision and subsequent flawless multi-year construction execution, not a cash-generating business — any of consent refusal, financing failure, cost overruns, or construction delay would be severely value-destructive

High-profile, sustained public and environmental opposition (Sam Neill, Helen Clark, Environmental Defence Society, local iwi) creates ongoing headline and political risk even within a fast-track statutory framework nominally designed to limit exactly this kind of contestation

Extreme sensitivity to the gold price cuts both ways — the PFS's own tornado analysis shows gold price is the single largest driver of NPV; a material pullback from current elevated gold prices toward or below the A$3,500/oz base case would sharply compress both the project's economics and the stock's valuation multiple simultaneously
